note: Phase 6 authoritative execution manifest for collaboration, presence, same-field conflict resolution, same-surface resolver behavior, and local pending queue semantics.

ledger.title: Phase 6 Coverage Ledger
notes: Sprint 0 activates the Phase 6 ownership map before feature work. Initial later-sprint rows are selectable placeholders until their owning behavior is implemented.

Phase 3 remains owner for server-side field-level patch rebase, same-field conflict transport, and collection conflict values. Phase 6 owns resolver, concurrent-client, and local pending-queue behavior.
authoritative_execution: `backend-unit` selects pure Phase 6 socket, conflict, and resolver-contract rows through the Phase 6 manifest and `backend_unit` execution dependency.
`backend-store` selects service-backed Phase 6 workbook mutation rows through manifest-owned store-domain selection.
`frontend-unit` selects Phase 6 workbook resolver, save-state, and pending-queue component rows through the Phase 6 manifest for `frontend_unit`.
`backend-integration` selects Phase 6 real-runtime WebSocket and concurrent-edit rows through the Phase 6 manifest and `backend_integration` execution dependency.
`browser-e2e-webserver-backed` carries authoritative `E-6-*` rows through duration-balanced Playwright manifest-entry shards under `browser_functional`.
support_execution_extras: Existing Phase 1 and Phase 3 socket, revocation, autosave, and same-field conflict tests remain carryover support evidence and must not claim Phase 6 IDs.
shared_harness: | Incident WebSocket helpers | `internal/testutil/incidentwstest` already owns canonical incident WebSocket handshakes and revocation assertions. Sprint 0 does not extend it; resume and replay-specific helpers belong with the real Sprint 2 tests. |
| Workbook resolver helpers | `apps/web/src/WorkbookShell.phase6.test.tsx` holds Phase 6 resolver, save-state, and pending-queue component rows until the UI is split into smaller owner components. |
| Browser collaboration helpers | `apps/web/e2e/phase6.collaboration.spec.ts` holds Phase 6 multi-client browser rows for presence, resolver UX, live-cell anchoring, and pending-queue recovery. |
support_only: `internal/modules/auth/phase1_integration_test.go` keeps Phase 1 session revocation socket coverage as carryover support for Phase 6 implementation, but authoritative Phase 6 completion claims must live in `phase6_*` rows.

`internal/modules/timeline/phase3_integration_test.go` keeps Phase 3 canonical socket and same-field conflict transport coverage as carryover support for Phase 6 implementation, but authoritative Phase 6 completion claims must live in `phase6_*` rows.

`internal/modules/workbook/workbook_mutation_integration_test.go` keeps existing workbook mutation conflict coverage as carryover support for Phase 6 implementation, but authoritative Phase 6 completion claims must live in `phase6_*` rows.

`apps/web/src/WorkbookShell.phase3.autosave.test.tsx` keeps Phase 3 autosave and conflict UI coverage as carryover support for Phase 6 implementation, but authoritative Phase 6 completion claims must live in `phase6_*` rows.

unit.claim: Every grid write includes `record_id`, `base_row_version`, and changed fields only; different-field concurrent edits auto-rebase, while same-field concurrent edits reject with an explicit conflict payload.
unit.out_of_scope: Same-surface resolver UX and local pending-queue replay behavior remain separate Phase 6 rows.

unit.claim: Same-field conflict transport uses `409`, `error.code='same_field_conflict'`, and an `error.conflict` object with the required base and current values.
unit.out_of_scope: Phase 3 remains owner for existing Timeline conflict transport support evidence; Phase 6 owns generalized resolver-consumable coverage.

unit.claim: `text_compare_merge` treats the field as plain text, normalizes line endings only for merge computation, and never silently auto-commits a clean merge suggestion.
unit.out_of_scope: Browser presentation of suggested merge choices remains resolver UI evidence.

unit.claim: `collection_review` fields use `collection_value_v1` in read or conflict payloads and `collection_actions_v1` in explicit resolution writes.
unit.out_of_scope: Interactive resolver choice rendering remains frontend evidence.

unit.title: Phase 6 U-6-05 keeps the grid visible, conflict unresolved, and focus bound to the same cell
unit.claim: The resolver keeps the grid visible, leaves conflict state unresolved until explicit action, and returns focus to the same cell after resolution or clear.
unit.out_of_scope: Backend same-field conflict payload construction remains backend evidence.

unit.title: Phase 6 U-6-06 applies explicit resolver outcomes to local conflict state and revisions
unit.claim: `keep_saved` clears the local conflict without creating a new revision, while `use_unsaved` and `merged_value` create a new attributed change set.
unit.out_of_scope: Low-level mutation persistence and audit attribution remain backend evidence.

unit.claim: The first application message on the incident socket is exactly one of `hello` or `resume`, and resume outside the replay window yields reset behavior rather than partial replay.
unit.out_of_scope: Presence snapshot and revocation close behavior are owned by `U-6-08` and integration rows.

unit.claim: Presence payloads are incident-scoped and ephemeral; heartbeats do not extend idle expiry; `session_revoked` closes the socket with the route-owned reason code set.
unit.out_of_scope: Real browser-origin rejection and two-client resume behavior remain integration evidence.

unit.title: Phase 6 U-6-09 keeps save-state labels and pending queue replay bounded and explicit
unit.claim: Save-state labels use only `Syncing`, `Saved`, and `Conflict`; the local pending queue is FIFO, bounded, coalesces only contiguous same-record units, and halts on blocking failures without silent eviction or reload restore.

integration.claim: Two real clients connect to the same incident socket, exchange presence snapshots and deltas, and observe deterministic replay ordering within the replay window.
integration.out_of_scope: Browser rendering of presence indicators remains `E-6-01` evidence.

integration.claim: Resume with a valid replay token replays replayable messages only, while presence is rehydrated through the documented presence flow rather than replay.
integration.out_of_scope: Low-level replay filtering helper behavior remains unit evidence.

integration.claim: Concurrent edits to different fields succeed without operator intervention, while concurrent edits to the same field produce the resolver path and preserve both saved and local drafts correctly.
integration.out_of_scope: Full browser resolver interaction remains `E-6-02` evidence.

integration.claim: Cookie-authenticated browser socket upgrades reject untrusted `Origin` values before incident subscription is granted.
integration.out_of_scope: General host and origin policy helpers remain platform support evidence.

e2e.title: E-6-01 shows two analysts each other's workbook presence within the expected interaction window
e2e.claim: Two analysts on the same incident see each other's presence on the workbook surface within the expected interaction window.
e2e.out_of_scope: Socket-level presence canonicalization remains backend evidence.

e2e.title: E-6-02 auto-merges different-field concurrent edits and requires explicit same-field resolution
e2e.claim: Concurrent edits to different fields on the same row auto-merge, while concurrent edits to the same field open the same-surface resolver and require explicit analyst resolution.
e2e.out_of_scope: Resolver state unit behavior remains frontend-unit evidence.

e2e.title: E-6-03 preserves unsaved local work after socket revocation and re-authentication
e2e.claim: Logout, expiry, or concurrency-limit revocation emits `session_revoked`, closes the socket, and preserves unsaved local work for later explicit recovery after re-authentication.
e2e.out_of_scope: Low-level session revocation socket delivery remains backend evidence.

e2e.title: E-6-04 keeps live updates and conflict markers anchored to record_id and field_key
e2e.claim: Live updates never retarget a pending local edit away from the bound `record_id` and `field_key` during sorting, filtering, grouping, virtual scrolling, or live row patch.
e2e.out_of_scope: Low-level grid adapter identity helpers may receive separate frontend unit coverage.

e2e.title: E-6-05 replays queued unsent writes after re-authentication without silent reload restore
e2e.claim: Within one browser runtime, queued unsent writes survive transient disconnect or session revocation, replay in FIFO order after re-authentication, halt on the first blocking non-retryable failure, and are never silently restored after a full reload.
e2e.out_of_scope: Queue size and coalescing unit semantics remain frontend-unit evidence.
